BufferSortKey::LastUsed over Document::focused_at, descending. Upstream labels the mapping 'By modification' but comparator.modified compares getbufinfo().lastused, not the modified flag — verified against astrocore/lua/astrocore/buffer/comparator.lua — so this ports the behaviour, not the label.

BufferSortKey::RelativePath sorts on Document::relative_path, which is what the buffer line displays. Home moves to the start of the command line (zmax-term/src/ui/prompt.rs:3220, self.move_start()). C-a does NOT, under the default vim presets: the guarded arm above it (prompt.rs:3216-3219, `ctrl!('a') if cx.editor.vim_semantics`) is vim's c_CTRL-A, which inserts every completion match. vim_semantics defaults to true (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:2548), so dte's C-a spelling is only available in the Emacs presets.

Left moves one character left on the command line (zmax-term/src/ui/prompt.rs:3210). C-b does not under the default vim presets: prompt.rs:3209 (`ctrl!('b') if cx.editor.vim_semantics`) is vim's c_CTRL-B and jumps to the start of the line; vim_semantics defaults to true (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:2548). dte's C-b spelling is Emacs-preset only.

All three leave the Ex line: Esc/C-g abort the prompt and C-c aborts the completion/prompt in the same handler (zmax-term/src/ui/prompt.rs, prompt.rs:2911-2914 for C-c and Esc, prompt.rs:3115 for C-g during an incremental search and prompt.rs:2908 in a recursive history read).

Delete deletes forward on the command line (zmax-term/src/ui/prompt.rs:3267-3270). C-d does not under the default vim presets: prompt.rs:3264-3266 is vim's c_CTRL-D, which lists matching names without changing the line; vim_semantics defaults to true (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:2548), so dte's C-d spelling only deletes in the Emacs presets.
C-e and End move to the end of the command line (zmax-term/src/ui/prompt.rs:3212).
C-f and Right move one character right (zmax-term/src/ui/prompt.rs:3211).
C-k deletes from the cursor to the end of the command line (zmax-term/src/ui/prompt.rs:3243-3246); the killed text goes to the prompt's kill store for C-y (prompt.rs:56).
C-u deletes from the cursor back to the start of the command line (zmax-term/src/ui/prompt.rs:3247-3250).
C-w, C-Backspace and M-Backspace all erase the word before the cursor — one match arm (zmax-term/src/ui/prompt.rs:3235-3238), exactly dte's three chords.
M-d, C-Delete and M-Delete all delete the word after the cursor — one match arm (zmax-term/src/ui/prompt.rs:3239-3242), exactly dte's three chords.
Tab on the Ex line completes the command or argument (zmax-term/src/ui/prompt.rs:3351-3354; S-Tab at 3355 walks back through the candidates).
Up/Down on the Ex line walk the prompt history — the handler maps M-p/C-p/Up/S-Up and M-n/C-n/Down/S-Down onto the history ring (zmax-term/src/ui/prompt.rs:3340-3350).

:quit / :q closes the current view (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:50804) — dte C-q.
:write / :w writes changes to disk (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:55213) — dte C-s.

'Move cursor and select whole words': extend_next_word_start / extend_prev_word_start extend the selection by a word in each direction (the extend twins of move_next_word_start / move_prev_word_start, which are already mapped as dte word-fwd / word-bwd). zmax leaves C-S-left/right unbound; the commands are what dte's keys run. Registered: `extend_prev_word_start` at zmax-term/src/commands.rs:435; `extend_next_word_start` at zmax-term/src/commands.rs:434.

'Move cursor and select whole lines': extend_line_below is 'Select current line, if already selected, extend to next line' and extend_line_above is its upward twin — repeated presses grow a linewise selection, which is what C-S-up/C-S-down do in dte. Registered: `extend_line_above` at zmax-term/src/commands.rs:778; `extend_line_below` at zmax-term/src/commands.rs:777.
:new creates a new scratch buffer (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:55261) — dte's C-t / C-n 'Open new buffer', and the same command mcedit EditNew is mapped to.
paste_clipboard_before — the command already mapped for dte's `paste` and mcedit Paste. Registered: `paste_clipboard_before` at zmax-term/src/commands.rs:1384.
:buffer-close closes the current buffer (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:54920) — dte C-w, and the command already mapped for dte's `close`.
cut_to_clipboard — the command already mapped for dte's `cut` and mcedit Cut. Registered: `cut_to_clipboard` at zmax-term/src/commands.rs:1222.
redo 'Redo change'. Registered: `redo` at zmax-term/src/commands.rs:1274.
undo 'Undo change'. Registered: `undo` at zmax-term/src/commands.rs:1272.
search_next 'Select next search match' — dte F3. Registered: `search_next` at zmax-term/src/commands.rs:520.
search_prev 'Select previous search match' — dte F4. Registered: `search_prev` at zmax-term/src/commands.rs:521.
command_mode 'Enter command mode' opens zmax's Ex line (typed::command_mode, reached from commands.rs:11541), which is the prompt dte's M-x opens; every dte `command` item is typed there.

The primitives are there: extend_char_left/right (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:3395-3401) and extend_line_up/down (commands.rs:3403-3409) move the cursor keeping the anchor. The shifted arrows are NOT them by default — S-up/S-down run page_up/page_down and S-left/S-right run subword_b/subword_w (shift_*_key, commands.rs:3182-3200), because 'keymodel' is empty by default (vim_options_data.rs:183). `:set keymodel=startsel` enters Select mode and routes the chords to the extend commands (keymodel_startsel, commands.rs:3049-3058), which is what makes them behave the dte way.
Enter accepts the search prompt and performs the search (zmax-term/src/ui/prompt.rs:3317); zmax searches by regex by default, which is dte's plain Enter.
M-c during a search is isearch_toggle_case (zmax-term/src/ui/prompt.rs:3155) — emacs isearch-toggle-case-fold, i.e. dte's 'Toggle case-sensitive-search option'.

dte's M-Enter runs the search escaped as plain text. zmax gets there by turning regexp matching off — M-r calls isearch_toggle(IsearchToggle::Regexp) (zmax-term/src/ui/prompt.rs:3156-3162, flag flipped at prompt.rs:2108-2115) and then Enter — a mode toggle plus accept rather than a second accept key. zmax's own M-Enter is minibuffer-choose-completion (prompt.rs:3016).

Reversing a running search is C-r — isearch_repeat(cx, false) at zmax-term/src/ui/prompt.rs:3095 — but only in the Emacs presets: the arm is guarded by isearch_ctl = isearch && !vim_semantics (prompt.rs:2888) and vim_semantics defaults to true (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:2548). In the default preset C-r inserts a register (prompt.rs:3377-3396) and the backwards search is a separate prompt (`?` / rsearch), so there is no key that flips the direction of the search in flight.

On SIGHUP a changed buffer is written out and the editor exits (zmax-term/src/application.rs:1198-1209, :1228-1244), and nothing is written to the remembered file. It differs from ed in where the rescue copy lands: zmax writes each modified buffer to its vim swap file (crate::vim_swap::preserve, recovered with :recover), not to a single `ed.hup` in the current directory. A buffer with no file name therefore gets no rescue copy at all, where ed's ed.hup would still capture it.

An interrupt returns to command mode instead of quitting: Application::interrupt (zmax-term/src/application.rs:1255-1305) cancels any half-typed chord (EditorView::cancel_pending_keys) and then runs the same command sequences C-c is bound to per mode in keymap/vim.rs:2832,2846 -- mark_insert_exit + normal_mode from insert, so the text already typed is committed to the buffer and its history as if input had ended normally. Partial: zmax has no ed-style `?` error line, so nothing is printed.

the terminal's resize event is handled in the event loop (zmax-term/src/application.rs:1353-1363 termina WindowResized, :1390-1403 TerminalEvent::Resize), which resizes the compositor and re-renders; `:redraw` forces the same re-render on demand.

`.` resolves to the cursor line (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66744 `"" | "." => cur`). ex ranges are resolved by resolve_filter_range's `addr` closure (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66735-66785) and fed to every ranged ex command — `:{range}s` (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66880-66906), `:{range}d`/`:{range}y` (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:67067-67124), `:{range}g` (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66945-66961), `:{range}j`, `:{range}!`, `:{range}sort`. A bare `:.` also moves the cursor (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66822-66845).

`?re?` is the same path with forward=false (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66673), searching backwards and wrapping to the end of the buffer. `??` now repeats the last search through the same last-search-register reuse as `//` (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66779-66802), and `:?re` with the closing delimiter omitted moves the cursor (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66961-66974).

`$` resolves to the last real line (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66745, `last_real_line` zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66517-66525, which excludes ropey's phantom line after a trailing newline). ex ranges are resolved by resolve_filter_range's `addr` closure (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66735-66785) and fed to every ranged ex command — `:{range}s` (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66880-66906), `:{range}d`/`:{range}y` (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:67067-67124), `:{range}g` (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66945-66961), `:{range}j`, `:{range}!`, `:{range}sort`.

ed's `^` synonym for `-` is now accepted: split_leading_range treats `^` as a range character (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66603) and the address parser reads it as a negative offset term, base split included (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66866, :66887, :66893). A bare `^` is the previous line and repeats accumulate (`^^` = -2), matching the existing `-` behaviour. Test caret_is_a_synonym_for_minus_in_addresses (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:69260).

`^N` (N-th previous line) runs through the same offset loop as `-N` now that `^` is a recognised sign (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66887-66893); `:^3,$d` parses (test at zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:69260).
`+` = next line: a bare `+` counts as 1 (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66760-66762 `if end == 0 { 1 }`), and repeats accumulate (`.++`).
`+N` via the offset loop (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66751-66766).

an omitted side of `a1,a2` is now the ed/sam default instead of the current line (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66912-66920): empty a1 -> line 1 (index 0), empty a2 -> `$`. A bare `,` therefore resolves to (0, last), identical to `%` (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66905-66907), so `:,d` / `:,s/a/b/` act on the whole buffer. Regression test omitted_comma_address_defaults_to_first_and_last_line (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:69197) asserts `,` == `%`, plus `,5` == 0,5 and `5,` == 5,$.

`;` is now an address separator: split_leading_range accepts it (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66603) and resolve_semicolon_list (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66821-66847) walks the `;`-separated list left to right, moving the current line to each address before the next is evaluated (ed's extract_addr_range), keeping the last two as the range. An omitted address before a `;` is the current line and an omitted one after the last `;` is `$`, so a bare `;` is `.,$`. Because the split happens before pattern substitution (split_semicolon_address zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66703-66732 skips `/re/`/`?re?` bodies), `/a/;/b/` searches for `b` from the `a` line, not from the cursor. Test semicolon_moves_the_current_line_between_addresses (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:69215).

`/re/` resolves to the next matching line, wrapping to the top (search_line_for_pattern zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66734-66760). Two gaps closed: an empty `//` now repeats the last search - the address resolver reuses the last-search register, the same one `:s//rep/` reuses (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66779-66790), and fails the address when there is no previous pattern (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66798-66802) instead of compiling `Regex::new("")`, which matched every line and silently resolved to the adjacent one; and a bare `:/re` / `:/re/` with no command now moves the cursor to the match, the closing delimiter being optional at end of line (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66961-66974).

`:k x` / `:mark x` sets the mark; `'x` in a range is replaced by its 1-based line before the numeric resolver runs (substitute_marks zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66594-66614), so `:'a,'bd` works. ed writes the same `'lc` syntax.
a bare `:N` is routed to `goto` (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66809-66813); as a range component `N` is parsed 1-based (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:66748 `n.parse::<usize>()?.checked_sub(1)`).

Eight divergences from autorevert.el. Five previously noted: path-keyed global state instead of buffer-local; no undo-boundary around the append; no before-save-hook auto-disable; upstream's trailing (setq auto-revert-mode nil) is not mirrored onto config.auto_reload, so with auto_reload on a whole-buffer reload can race the tail append; the modified-buffer y-or-n-p is absent; plus a toggle-off/on within one 5s tick leaves two concurrent auto_revert_tail_loop tasks racing (commands.rs:14811 only exits when it observes the key missing). Three additional, found here: (1) upstream seeds tail-pos only via (or (local-variable-p 'auto-revert-tail-pos) (setq-local …)) and never unsets it when the mode turns off, so disable then re-enable resumes from the stale offset and appends what was written meanwhile — commands.rs:14796 removes the map entry and 14800 re-seeds from the current file size,…

Real emacs word semantics, not vim's. `emacs -Q --batch` over "foo.bar baz_qux  end" reports forward-word stopping at 3, 7, 11, 15, 20 and backward-word at 17, 12, 8, 4, 0 -- so a word is a run of ALPHANUMERICS (`_` is a symbol constituent in every shipped mode, which is why it stops inside `baz_qux`), forward lands after the word and backward on its first character. vim's `w`/`b`, which these used to be bound to, count `_` as a word char and stop on punctuation runs emacs skips. emacs_word_step / emacs_word_target (zmax-term/src/commands.rs) reproduce both stop sequences exactly, asserted against those probed numbers, and the emacs preset's M-f/M-b are bound to them (with extend_forward_word / extend_backward_word for an active mark).

The third cwarn.el check is in. The old note said it needed the callee's declaration; it does not -- cwarn-font-lock-match-reference (cwarn.el:305) is purely syntactic: the regexp `[^&]\\(&\\)[^&=]`, backward-up-list landing on `(`, and c-at-toplevel-p. cwarn_reference_scan (zmax-core/src/cmode.rs) implements exactly that, modelling toplevel with a brace stack in which class/struct/union/namespace/extern open a declaration level (cc-engine's "directly inside a class, namespace or other block that contains another declaration level"), skipping comments and string/char literals so they neither nest nor fire, and reusing the existing in-macro test. It is C++-only, per cwarn-configuration's `((c-mode (not reference)) (c++-mode t))`, which the new CWarnLang carries. Five tests: the flag itself, `&&`/`&=` non-matches, the paren-and-macro conditions, toplevel vs function body vs class member, and literals.

`diary-hebrew-birthday` is ported against cal-hebrew.el:774-799. `DateSpec::HebrewBirthday { birth: Date, after_sunset: bool }` stores a CIVIL birth date and `hebrew_birthday` (zmax-core/src/diary.rs:1384) converts it with `hebrew_from_fixed(rd(birth) + after_sunset)`, matching Emacs's `(calendar-hebrew-from-absolute (+ (calendar-absolute-from-gregorian ...) (if after-sunset 1 0)))`; the three date args follow `calendar-date-style`. The optional 4th AFTER-SUNSET arg parses (absent/`nil` false, `t` true) and shifts the birth one civil day. Results render through `hebrew_birthday_string` as Emacs's `"%s's %d%s Hebrew birthday%s"` with ordinal suffix and a " (evening)" marker on the day-before match, reached from `Entry::display_text`, so all six diary listing commands emit the formatted line. Verified by driving zmax-core against live `emacs -Q --batch`: 23/23 probes match, covering the civil-vs-Hebrew discriminator (civil 1990-04-10 fires 2026-04-01 evening / 04-02 and NOT 2026-07-26), both AFTER-SUNSET shifts, ordinals 1st/2nd/3rd/11th/21st/22nd/31st/36th/100th, American/European/ISO date styles, the leap-year Adar branch (civil 1990-03-12 -> 2027-03-23 evening / 03-24), and the `age > 0` guard.

Not yet observed: the M-x `diary-hebrew-birthday` command itself (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:21623). Its source filters today's HebrewBirthday entries and reports `display_text`, falling back to "No Hebrew birthday today (<hebrew date>)", and the display_text path underneath it is verified -- but the workspace binary could not be built during verification (3 unrelated compile errors in zmax-term from concurrent work, plus a stale prebuilt binary), so the command's live behavior is unconfirmed.

Still divergent, separate spec: `diary-hebrew-yahrzeit` continues to read its args as a Hebrew date, accepts no AFTER-SUNSET, and prints the raw entry text instead of Emacs's "NAME's Nth yahrzeit" formatting.

Full port of cal-hebrew.el:858-920, whose docstring is "Entry applies if date is Rosh Hodesh, the day before, or the Saturday before" -- three different days, where zmax answered only the first and only with the month name. Now: the `(and (= h-day 1) (/= h-month 7))` exclusion, so 1 Tishri is Rosh Hashanah and gets no entry; the `(first day)`/`(second day)` suffixes off the previous day's Hebrew day; `Erev Rosh Hodesh %s` on day 29 when the month is not 6; and both Saturday `Mevarchim Rosh Hodesh` arms, including the wrap to Nisan past the year's last month. Expected strings were generated from GNU Emacs 31.1 itself under `emacs -Q --batch`. The caller was prefixing its own "Rosh Hodesh ", which would have doubled the words and mislabelled the Erev and Mevarchim entries, so it now reports the entry verbatim. An existing test asserted the missing exclusion (1 Tishri -> Some("Tishri")) and was corrected.

Two defects fixed. (1) With point ABOVE the first hunk -- on the banner, the `---` or the `+++` -- the search was rposition-only and reported "no hunk at point"; emacs's (diff-beginning-of-hunk t) has a fallback chain of re-search-backward THEN re-search-forward, so it refines the FIRST hunk. hunk_bounds_at (zmax-core/src/diffmode.rs) implements that chain and ui/diffmode.rs calls it. (2) A `\\ No newline at end of file` marker between the `-` and `+` runs parses as context and ended the `-` run early, leaving the pair unrefined; refine_runs steps over it, as emacs does with diff--forward-while-leading-char. Both are pure and unit tested, including that a bare `+` run and an unpaired `-` run refine nothing (diff-refine-nonmodified is nil).

It goes through the real Info major mode now (Dired::show_as_info sets major_mode `info`, the same way commands::info_display_node does), which is where n (Info-next), p, u, l, d, t and RET live (keymap/major_mode.rs). `M-s a C-s` is dired-do-isearch, a LITERAL search; only `M-s a C-M-s` is the regexp form. Both arms armed the same regexp prompt, so a `.` or `*` in a literal search silently matched the wrong thing. The literal branch now passes `grep -F` -- the search shells out to grep, whose default dialect is POSIX BRE with GNU extensions, so regex-escaping the pattern would have turned `a+` into grep's own one-or-more operator and reintroduced the bug. The two prompts and the result header now name which search ran.

The regexp form, now distinguishable from the literal one (see dired-do-isearch), and its translator no longer emits patterns that misbehave: emacs_regexp_to_rust (zmax-term/src/ui/dired.rs) mapped `\\sw` to `\\s` plus a literal `w`, which COMPILED and matched whitespace-then-w -- a silent mismatch rather than an error. It now translates the two syntax classes with an exact analogue (`\\s-`/`\\s ` and `\\sw`, with complements) and returns None for everything it cannot express -- the other syntax classes, `\\cC` categories, and backreferences, which a finite automaton cannot support at all -- so the caller reports a bad pattern instead of holding point. Tested by compiling every translated pattern with regex::Regex::new.

emoji.el's emoji--name falls back to the character's UNICODE name, which is why emacs on `a` says 'The name of "a" is "LATIN SMALL LETTER A"' where zmax said it knew no name. That fallback exists now: a single-character glyph with no emoji-table entry is named from the Unicode database. There is a real Unicode name database now: zmax-core/src/unicode_names.txt, 32,948 listed names generated by scripts/gen_unicode_names.py from the Unicode Character Database (CPython's unicodedata, version recorded in the file). The 110,720 names Unicode DERIVES are computed rather than stored (UAX #44 name-derivation rules): NR1 composes the Hangul syllables from the jamo short names, NR2 is a fixed prefix plus the codepoint in hex for the CJK ideograph, Khitan and Nushu ranges -- held as the UCD's exact contiguous runs, not a min/max span, so a codepoint in a gap between runs is correctly nameless instead of borrowing a neighbour's prefix. Both directions are unit tested, including the case-insensitive match emacs's completion does and the fact that the jamo short names are not prefix-free (`GG` must beat `G`).

The old note described a scratch-buffer dump; the command is a real port. `M-f` in Dired reads emacs's two prompts in emacs's order -- "Run find in directory: " defaulting to the directory Dired is on, then "Run find (with args): " (find-dired.el:189-190) -- and runs `find . \\( ARGS \\)` through `sh -c` in that directory, so ARGS is shell-parsed and quoting, globs and `-o` alternations mean what find and the shell say they mean (find-dired.el:194 hands the line to start-file-process-shell-command for the same reason). Real emacs word semantics, not vim's. `emacs -Q --batch` over "foo.bar baz_qux  end" reports forward-word stopping at 3, 7, 11, 15, 20 and backward-word at 17, 12, 8, 4, 0 -- so a word is a run of ALPHANUMERICS (`_` is a symbol constituent in every shipped mode, which is why it stops inside `baz_qux`), forward lands after the word and backward on its first character. vim's `w`/`b`, which these used to be bound to, count `_` as a word char and stop on punctuation runs emacs skips. emacs_word_step / emacs_word_target (zmax-term/src/commands.rs) reproduce both stop sequences exactly, asserted against those probed numbers, and the emacs preset's M-f/M-b are bound to them (with extend_forward_word / extend_backward_word for an active mark).

Backend is NNTP over TCP (RFC 3977 MODE READER / LIST ACTIVE / GROUP / OVER / ARTICLE, std::net, zmax-term/src/gnus.rs) taken from $NNTPSERVER or the :gnus argument; with neither set it falls back to a local mbox spool at ~/News, one file per group. Connect and LIST ACTIVE run on a blocking task so the editor does not stall.

Emacs image-crop is an interactive rectangle editor: an SVG rectangle is overlaid on the image and adjusted with mouse-1 drag plus m (move), s (move, square-constrained), RET (execute), q (abort). zmax has none of that - the region must be typed as an ImageMagick WxH+X+Y geometry into an in-mode minibuffer (zmax-term/src/ui/image.rs:146-149, 190-234), because the picture is painted straight to the terminal by an external viewer with no cell to draw a rubber band into. Four concrete consequences, three of them not previously recorded: (1) No display-to-original scaling. image-crop.el computes factor = original_width / displayed_width and multiplies every rectangle coordinate by it before running the command, so the visual selection is always correct under scaling; zmax applies the typed geometry directly to the file's pixel space with no factor (image.rs:360-384), so once `i +`/`i -`…

Carried forward and re-verified from source: (a) the region is typed as a WxH+X+Y geometry into an in-mode minibuffer (`begin_input`, image.rs:151-153) instead of Emacs's SVG rectangle drag session (`image-crop--crop-image-1`) with its own q/RET/m/s loop; (b) the fill colour is an optional second whitespace-separated word (image.rs:353-357) rather than a C-u prefix arg feeding `read-color`; (c) `-fill` precedes `-draw`, so zmax honours a non-default colour whereas Emacs's own command ignores it and always fills black (verified with magick above) — zmax's output differs from Emacs's for any colour but "black"; (d) `image-crop--possibly-rotate-buffer` (ic.el:422) bakes the image's :rotation and :width into the data before the cut, while zmax cuts the untransformed original and applies IMAGE_XFORM only at redisplay; (e) Emacs binds i x via image-map for any image at point, zmax's…

"Read a character by its Unicode name and add it to the search string" (isearch.el). It read a two-key DIGRAPH mnemonic, so `a:` worked and LATIN SMALL LETTER A WITH DIAERESIS did not. There is a real Unicode name database now: zmax-core/src/unicode_names.txt, 32,948 listed names generated by scripts/gen_unicode_names.py from the Unicode Character Database (CPython's unicodedata, version recorded in the file). The 110,720 names Unicode DERIVES are computed rather than stored (UAX #44 name-derivation rules): NR1 composes the Hangul syllables from the jamo short names, NR2 is a fixed prefix plus the codepoint in hex for the CJK ideograph, Khitan and Nushu ranges -- held as the UCD's exact contiguous runs, not a min/max span, so a codepoint in a gap between runs is correctly nameless instead of borrowing a neighbour's prefix. Both directions are unit tested, including the case-insensitive match emacs's completion does and the fact that the jamo short names are not prefix-free (`GG` must beat `G`). The digraph mnemonics still resolve as a fallback, so vim's two-key form keeps working for anyone who reaches for it.

isearch_complete (zmax-term/src/commands.rs) is a port of isearch-complete1 (isearch.el:3415-3438), not the one-history-entry completion the old note described: it runs try_completion over the WHOLE search ring (zmax-core/src/search.rs try_completion_fold, with emacs's completion-ignore-case bound to case-fold-search), extends the search string on a longer shared prefix, reports the sole match unchanged, lists every candidate in a scratch buffer under emacs's "Possible completions are:" header when the candidates agree on nothing further, and says "No completion" when none match. It now also does what isearch-complete adds on top of complete1 (isearch.el:3440-3452): every branch that succeeds hands off to isearch_edit_string, so the completed string is editable in the minibuffer, and only the "No completion" branch skips it. One divergence remains: emacs completes a regexp search against regexp-search-ring and a literal one against search-ring, while zmax has a single search history (the `/` register, vim's) that both read.

keymap.el's own docstring settles the scope: "The binding goes in the current buffer's local keymap, which in most cases is shared with all other buffers in the same major mode." zmax's local keymap IS the major-mode overlay (zmax-term/src/keymap/major_mode.rs), so keymap_local_set stores the binding against the focused buffer's Document::major_mode() and every buffer in that mode sees it -- the same scope emacs describes, not an approximation. major_mode::overlay merges the runtime bindings over the shipped ones and Keymaps::get_with_language consults that overlay before the base keymap, so a local binding shadows both the shipped major-mode chord and the global map, as emacs's local map shadows the global one; a major mode with no shipped overlay gets one made (emacs's use-local-map on a buffer that had none). The key is read in emacs's own kbd notation (zmax_core::kbd::emacs_kbd_to_zmax) and the command name is validated before it reaches the map. The mirror of right-word: backward-word in a left-to-right paragraph. Real emacs word semantics, not vim's. `emacs -Q --batch` over "foo.bar baz_qux  end" reports forward-word stopping at 3, 7, 11, 15, 20 and backward-word at 17, 12, 8, 4, 0 -- so a word is a run of ALPHANUMERICS (`_` is a symbol constituent in every shipped mode, which is why it stops inside `baz_qux`), forward lands after the word and backward on its first character. vim's `w`/`b`, which these used to be bound to, count `_` as a word char and stop on punctuation runs emacs skips. emacs_word_step / emacs_word_target (zmax-term/src/commands.rs) reproduce both stop sequences exactly, asserted against those probed numbers, and the emacs preset's M-f/M-b are bound to them (with extend_forward_word / extend_backward_word for an active mark).

"Send the message in the current buffer" (message.el) -- and, unlike message-send-and-exit, keep the buffer. It queued unconditionally and reported "no SMTP configured", even though a real transport exists and its own sibling used it: send_current_draft (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:39307) assembles and validates the draft and hands it to sendmail(1) through send_via_sendmail (:39256), which is emacs's message-send-mail-with-sendmail. message_send now takes that path and falls back to the outbox queue only on a machine with no MTA, which is the same rule message-send-and-exit follows.

The helper the row assumed would already exist did not, so it was written here: `sendmail_program` (typed.rs:38875-38893) resolves Emacs' `sendmail-program` search order, and `send_via_sendmail` (typed.rs:38897-38934) pipes the assembled message to it with Emacs' own argv (`-oi`, `-f {From}`, `-oem -odb`, `-t`), treating a non-zero exit as a failed send. `send_current_draft` (typed.rs:38937-38950) validates and sends, returning None when the machine has no MTA. `message_send_and_exit` (typed.rs:38985-39004) now sends and only then runs buffer-close! — "Send message like `message-send', then, if no errors, exit from mail buffer", so a failed send leaves the draft on screen; with no MTA it falls back to the outbox queue and says so. `message_send` itself was deliberately left queueing: it is its own spec row (emacs.command.message_send) and now only has to call send_current_draft.  Upstream: GNU Emacs message.el:4321-4340 (`message-send-and-exit`), message.el:5082-5150 (`message-send-mail-with-sendmail` argv), sendmail.el:46-52 (`sendmail-program` default)

puts every installed package on the elisp load path and evaluates its autoload file. downloads <name>-<version>.tar (or .el) over HTTP, unpacks it into ~/.zmax/elpa/, and activates it by evaluating its <name>-autoloads.el (or <name>.el) in elisprs. Dependencies are resolved depth-first from the archive listing and installed before their dependants; 'emacs' is a host-version requirement, not a package, and is skipped, as is anything already installed at a new enough version

x: carries out the marks. Deletions remove the package directory; installations resolve dependencies and go through the download job, then activate. Marks are cleared and the rows rebuilt against what is now on disk, so a row flips available -> installed without a second network round trip
/ a: narrows to the packages one archive served (gnu, nongnu, melpa)
/ d: narrows the listing to packages whose summary contains the text
/ k: narrows to packages declaring the keyword (the :keywords the archive lists)
/ n: narrows the listing to packages whose name contains the text. Filters COMPOSE - each one narrows what the previous left - as they do in emacs
/ N: narrows to packages whose name OR summary contains the text
/ s: narrows by the Status column - installed, available, obsolete (a newer version is in the archive) or external (installed but in no archive, i.e. from a file or from VC)
/ v: narrows to packages whose version starts with the text
/ /: drops every filter, restoring the full listing
/ m: shows only the packages carrying a mark - what x is about to act on
/ u: shows only the packages that can be upgraded
H: hides the package under point from the listing
d: marks the package under point for deletion and steps down

~: marks for deletion every installed version that a newer INSTALLED version supersedes (distinct from U, which is about versions in the archive)
u (and DEL in the menu, which steps up instead of down): removes the mark from the package under point
U: marks every package the archive has a newer version of for installation - installing the newer version IS the upgrade

The point-context detector exists now, which is the whole command. prog_fill_reindent_defun (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:38926) asks comment_string_spans_in for a comment/string node containing the cursor; inside one it selects that span, runs reflow_selections (fill-paragraph) and collapses the selection back to a bare cursor, since M-q is not a selecting command; outside one it takes the tree-sitter `function` object (c_function_object — the same beginning-of-defun..end-of-defun span prog_indent_sexp's prefix case uses) and reindents those lines. A buffer with no grammar falls back to plain fill rather than erroring, so M-q keeps a meaning either way.

emacs's recover-session does not scan the disk for auto-save files: it reads the SESSION files written under auto-save-list-file-prefix, one per running emacs, each listing what that session auto-saved -- "This command first displays a Dired buffer showing you the previous sessions that you could recover from. To choose one [...] you'll be asked about a number of files to recover" (files.el:7522). zmax kept no such file, so it could only offer a flat scan of the directories it happened to be looking at. It writes them now: vim_swap records every (file, swap) pair it auto-saves into <cache>/auto-save-list/.saves-<pid>-<host>, in emacs's own format -- a pair of lines per buffer, the visited file then the auto-save file, an empty first line for a buffer visiting none (files.el recover-session-finish) -- rewriting it on each swap write so it stays correct when a clean save removes one. recover_session is the two-step command: sessions newest first with how long ago each was written (emacs sorts its listing with `-t` for the same reason), then that session's files, skipping any whose auto-save file is gone -- emacs's "Ignore a file if its auto-save file does not exist now." The old disk scan remains as the fallback for an editor that died before its first auto-save, or a swap directory written by something else. The session format's parse is unit tested, including the empty-first-line case, a truncated trailing pair and a missing auto-save name.

emacs's right-word is "(if (eq (current-bidi-paragraph-direction) 'left-to-right) (forward-word n) (backward-word n))". zmax renders left-to-right, so it is forward-word -- now a real port of emacs's word semantics rather than vim's `w`. Real emacs word semantics, not vim's. `emacs -Q --batch` over "foo.bar baz_qux  end" reports forward-word stopping at 3, 7, 11, 15, 20 and backward-word at 17, 12, 8, 4, 0 -- so a word is a run of ALPHANUMERICS (`_` is a symbol constituent in every shipped mode, which is why it stops inside `baz_qux`), forward lands after the word and backward on its first character. vim's `w`/`b`, which these used to be bound to, count `_` as a word char and stop on punctuation runs emacs skips. emacs_word_step / emacs_word_target (zmax-term/src/commands.rs) reproduce both stop sequences exactly, asserted against those probed numbers, and the emacs preset's M-f/M-b are bound to them (with extend_forward_word / extend_backward_word for an active mark).

rmail-resend now synthesises the headers that make it a RESEND rather than a forward: resend_fields_to (zmax-core/src/rmail.rs) emits Resent-From, Resent-Date (RFC 5322 format), Resent-To and Resent-Message-ID ahead of the original headers and body, and strips Sender: -- "Delete any Sender field, since that's not specifiable" (rmail.el:4161-4172). The original message goes out unaltered and the Resent-* set records the new hop (RFC 5322 3.6.6). The address is read BEFORE the draft is built, because Resent-To: carries it: emacs's spec is `(interactive "sResend to: ")`, and both the `R` key in the reader and the command run by name prompt for it. set-justification-none is `unjustify-region` THEN `fill-region` (fill.el:1274-1276) -- it UNDOES justification. zmax's Justification::None arm was `line.trim_end()`, so after a full/right/center justify it left the stretched inter-word gaps and the leading pad exactly where they were, i.e. it did nothing. unjustify_block (zmax-core/src/text_engine.rs) refills paragraph-at-a-time through fill_paragraph with an empty prefix, which drops the leading pad (unjustify-current-line's center/right arm) and collapses the stretched runs (its full arm, canonically-space-region) before refilling to width; blank lines break the paragraph and pass through. Tested by round-tripping real Full/Right/Center output back through None. An existing test was asserting the defect (a surviving three-space pad) and now asserts the pad is gone.

"Set VARIABLE to VALUE. [...] When called interactively, the user is prompted for VARIABLE and then VALUE" (simple.el:9980-10010). set_variable (zmax-term/src/commands.rs) is those two prompts -- "Set variable: " with completion over the settings, then emacs's "Set <var> to value: ", which names the variable it is setting -- over zmax's user options, which are its config settings: the same universe describe-variable reports on. The type check emacs gets from the defcustom declaration is the config's own deserialization, reached by routing the write through the :set-option implementation so the parse, the check and the live config update stay one code path; a value that will not parse into the setting's type is rejected by field name and the setting is left alone.

What separates it from setq is that it runs the option's custom-set function and warns when the value does not match the declared type. `:set-option NAME VALUE` is that: the value is parsed into the setting's own type through the config's deserialization and rejected by field name when it does not fit, then installed through the live ConfigEvent::Update path rather than written straight into the struct.

"Run TeX on the current region, via a temporary file. [...] If the buffer has a header, the header is given to TeX before the region itself. The buffer's header is all lines between the strings defined by tex-start-of-header and tex-end-of-header inclusive. The header must start in the first 100 lines of the buffer. The value of tex-trailer is given to TeX as input after the region" (tex-mode.el:2567-2579). It used to compile the whole file, which is tex-buffer. tex_region_source (zmax-term/src/commands.rs) builds the source emacs builds: the header -- latex-mode's tex-start-of-header `\\document(style|class)` through its tex-end-of-header `\\begin\\s-*{document}`, inclusive, and only when it starts within the first 100 lines -- then the region, then the `\\end{document}` trailer. A buffer with no header contributes none, which is emacs's already-output 0 case, and the trailer is still supplied so TeX sees a complete document. The temp file is written beside the buffer's own, which is what tex-directory defaulting to "." gets you and what makes a relative \\input in the region resolve, and tex_run_file runs the tool on it through the same one-job-at-a-time plumbing tex-buffer uses. Five unit tests: both header spellings, a spaced `\\begin {document}`, the 100-line limit, the headerless case, and that the trailer lands on its own line whether or not the region ended in a newline.

Emacs scopes toggle-frame-tab-bar to the SELECTED frame -- it sets that frame's `tab-bar-lines` -- where tab-bar-mode sets the parameter on every frame. zmax's was the global mode, so the bar could not be up on one frame and down on another. FrameState carries a `tab_bar: Option<bool>` override now: Some wins over the global mode for that frame, None follows it, and the renderer reads it through Editor::frame_tab_bar at the one place the bufferline's visibility is decided (zmax-term/src/ui/editor.rs). The override is carried forward when a frame is parked, a new frame starts with None so it follows the mode, and tab-bar-mode calls clear_frame_tab_bars so the global mode really governs every frame again -- which is what setting the parameter on all of them amounts to. The IDE workbench still forces the row it reserves for its own tabs. Tested in zmax-view: the override sticks to one frame, survives being parked and displayed again, does not leak to a frame made later, and is cleared wholesale by the global mode.

Because deactivating drops the half-typed key sequence, C-\ C-\ between two characters stops them combining, as the manual describes. The shipped vim/spacemacs preset keeps vim's CTRL-\ CTRL-N prefix on C-\, so the key binding is in the emacs preset; the command itself runs from M-x in every preset.

Emacs keeps two commands apart here: scroll-bar-mode sets every frame and the default for new ones, while toggle-scroll-bar acts on the SELECTED frame -- and zmax's toggle-scroll-bar just called scroll-bar-mode, so it could not be on for one frame and off for another. The side is a frame parameter now (`vertical-scroll-bars`): FrameState carries it, snapshot_current_frame captures the live value when a frame is parked and restore_frame applies the target frame's when it is displayed again, a new frame inherits the current setting the way default-frame-alist supplies an un-overridden parameter, and toggle_scroll_bar records the flip against the displayed frame (Editor::set_frame_scroll_bar) so it sticks without needing a switch. scroll-bar-mode is unchanged and still global.

xref-go-back is the current name for xref-pop-marker-stack, and it now pops the xref ring rather than the jumplist. There is a real xref marker ring now, and it is deliberately NOT the jumplist: vim's jumplist records every jump -- searches, `G`, `%`, a window change -- so popping it after a definition lookup lands wherever the last unrelated jump happened to be, which is the divergence the old note recorded. XREF_MARKERS (zmax-term/src/commands.rs) is a ring only xref pushes to, bounded at emacs's xref-marker-ring-length of 16 with the oldest falling off, and every xref entry point pushes the invocation point as it jumps: goto_impl's single-location arm, its picker's selection callback -- pushed there rather than when the picker opens, so a cancelled pick leaves the ring alone -- and the etags/ggtags path, which is what xref-etags-mode makes `M-.` resolve through. Popping skips markers into buffers that have since been closed, as emacs's markers into a killed buffer are dead, and an empty ring reports "At start of xref history". Unit tested for the bound and the LIFO order.

That is Emacs's contract for the mode, but the destination differs — there is no live WebKit widget, so the characters land in the rendered text rather than in a web form.

an incremental search over the page: typing extends the query and moves the cursor to the match, C-s shows the next result and C-r the previous one, both wrap, the prompt reads "failing" when there is no match, and RET/Esc exit. Not the real thing: it searches the rendered text, not the WebKit widget's own find machinery, so matches in content the text renderer drops (alt text, script, hidden elements) are not found and results are not highlighted in a page layout.

puts the WebKit buffer's one-key command map over the current buffer (g browse-url, r reload, b/f back/forward, w current-url, H browse-history, e edit-mode, C-s/C-r isearch-mode, q quit) and takes it off again when re-run, the way image-mode doubles as its own toggle. Not the real thing: it is a keymap over a text-rendered page, not the major mode of a live WebKit widget, so xwidget-webkit-scroll-*, zoom and adjust-size have no widget to act on and are not bound — ordinary buffer motions scroll the page instead.

zmax scales the whole terminal, not the buffer. `text_scale_decrease` (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:38947) mutates one global `editor.text_scale` counter and calls `emit_font_step(-1)` (commands.rs:38924-38934) which writes xterm `OSC 50 ;#-1` — a terminal-wide font-menu step, so every window/pane changes together and emacs's buffer-local `text-scale-mode` face-height (two windows at different scales) is unreachable. Terminals with no font menu ignore the sequence, so the command can be a pure no-op while still printing `text scale: -1`. Two further gaps the first skeptic missed: (a) the counter is unbounded while the terminal's font menu clamps at its smallest entry, so `editor.text_scale` desyncs from the real font and `text_scale_apply`/`text_scale_set` (commands.rs:61451-61466), which compute deltas from that counter, then step the wrong amount; (b) the C-wheel branch is only reached…

Three gaps. (a) Effect is not per-buffer text scaling at all: text_scale_increase (commands.rs:38939) bumps one global editor.text_scale counter and emits terminal-wide OSC 50 #+1 (emit_font_step, commands.rs:38926); nothing reads editor.text_scale except the text_scale_set/adjust/mode bookkeeping (commands.rs:61445-61510), no renderer consults it, and emit_font_step's own doc says terminals without a font menu ignore the sequence — so on most terminals C-wheel-up produces only the status line "text scale: +1". The counter is also shared in effect with frame_zoom_in/out (commands.rs:38966+), which drive the same OSC steps, so the two families interfere and text_scale_reset resets globally rather than per window. emacs mouse-wheel-text-scale scales only the buffer in the window under the pointer. (b) Unadmitted runtime shadow: bufferline_y is initialized to 0 (ui/editor.rs:446) and only…

UNVERIFIED AND NOT RUNNABLE: none of this has ever been executed. The built binary predates the edits (C-x 4 is unbound there; the old code still goes 2 windows -> 3, reproduced under pty), and the working tree does not compile, so the reuse path has not been driven even once.

KNOWN DIVERGENCES THAT REMAIN:
- >=3 windows: emacs reuses the next window in cyclic order (verified: with focus on the middle of 3, emacs reused the window below and left the first alone). `views().find(|id| *id != focus)` picks the first view in arena order (tree.rs:608), so with focus off the arena-first view zmax replaces a different window's buffer than emacs. The two rules agree only at exactly 2 windows.
- Focus is moved when the picker OPENS; emacs reads the filename in its interactive spec with the original window still selected and switches only on RET. The abort end-state is restored, but the mid-prompt state differs.
- The workspace picker enumerates existing files, so it cannot visit a not-yet-existing path; emacs's prompt passes `confirm-nonexistent-file-or-buffer` and can.

C-x a i l is bound to inverse_add_mode_abbrev in the emacs preset (keymap/emacs.rs:254, committed in HEAD — not new this round). Driven end-to-end in a pty under `keymap = "emacs"` against GNU Emacs 30.2 as oracle, it matches abbrev.el's `inverse-add-abbrev` (lines 427-444) on four points: it prompts `Expansion for Mode abbrev "<name>": ` per abbrev.el:436; it stores the key downcased per `(define-abbrev table (downcase name) exp)` at :441 (verified observably — defining from `FOO` then expanding a typed lowercase `foo` hits); it runs the trailing `(save-excursion (goto-char end) (expand-abbrev))` at :442-444, replacing the word in-buffer with the expansion; and it honours `(interactive "p")` including negative counts, with C-u 2 / C-u 3 / C-u -1 selecting the same word as the oracle ("EXPANDED two", "XX bb cc", "aa ZZ cc").

Known divergence: the expansion is inserted verbatim. abbrev_do_expand (commands.rs:20739) applies the replacement as a plain Transaction with no case adjustment, so abbrev.el:865-884 — upcase-initials-region/upcase-region when the abbrev name is all-caps, capitalize-first-initial when it merely contains caps — is unported. `hello FOO` yields "hello fungible object" where emacs yields "hello Fungible Object"; `hello Foo` yields "hello fungible object" where emacs yields "hello Fungible object". Only all-lowercase abbrev names round-trip identically.

Unrelated but adjacent: C-e in the emacs preset leaves the cursor on the final character rather than past it (col 1:9 on a 9-char line), so a C-e-then-C-x-a-i-l sequence defines the wrong span ("fo" instead of "foo"). That belongs to the move-end-of-line binding, not to this command — with the cursor at true point-max this command is exact.

`C-x a l` is bound to `add_mode_abbrev` in the emacs preset's INSERT keymap (`C-x a i l` -> inverse), and the command ports abbrev.el's `add-abbrev` prompts and word-extraction faithfully: at an equal point position it reproduces emacs 30.2 byte-for-byte, including trailing whitespace — no-arg takes one word back, ARG>0 takes ARG words back, negative ARG prompts `Undefine Mode abbrev: `, an existing definition prompts `NAME expands into "EXP"; redefine? `, and the name is stored downcased. The region clause (ARG 0 / active region) is implemented and works when the region comes from `C-x h`.

It is NOT reachable the way emacs users reach it: `C-SPC` enters Select mode, whose keymap (keymap/emacs.rs:261-281) binds no `C-x` prefix, so `C-x a l` is inert with a region active. With no user region, ARG 0 silently defines a one-character abbrev from the helix block cursor instead of erroring `The mark is not set now`. `only-global-abbrevs` does not exist, so the redirect to the global table is unimplemented; mode tables are in-memory only (no `abbrev_file_name` persistence) and are keyed by document language / `fundamental` rather than an emacs major-mode name.

Unrelated to this command but affecting its documented workflow: `C-e` (`goto_line_end`) stops one character short of emacs `end-of-line`, so `C-e` then `C-x a l` captures a truncated expansion.

`C-x w d` is toggle_window_dedication, a real tri-state on the view: it drops any dedication first and applies the strong flag only when turning it on, echoing emacs's 'Window is {no longer|now|now strongly} dedicated to buffer %s' verbatim; a strongly dedicated window refuses a buffer switch and a weakly dedicated one causes display-buffer-style redirection into an existing other window. The prefix mapping matches emacs now: `(if (consp flag) t ...)` means only a *raw* `C-u` dedicates strongly, while a numeric prefix (or a leading count, the spacemacs/vim keymaps having no `C-u` prefix command) is a non-nil non-t FLAG - which `toggle-window-dedicated-flag`'s own docstring, read out of emacs 31.1, says gives "the same kind of non-strong dedication" as its default value `interactive`. It was the other way round: any leading count dedicated strongly and a bare `C-u` weakly. That docstring also settles the old note's second point: `interactive` is not a third dedication state, it is an ordinary non-strong one. `C-x z` is emacs `repeat`: it runs the *last command* again, whatever that was. `repeat_last_command` (commands.rs) replays the command the key dispatcher recorded in LAST_COMMAND — every dispatched command except the repeat itself, so `C-x z z z` keeps repeating the command that came before it. It then arms `repeat`'s own transient map through `emacs_repeat::arm_command_repeat`, which is not gated on `repeat-mode` (emacs installs that map from the command, mode or no mode), so a bare `z` repeats again. The chord used to run `repeat_last_motion`, which could only repeat a motion - an edit before it was not repeatable at all. `I` (`dired-do-info`) is bound and reachable. Dired's `handle_event` strips `KeyModifiers::SHIFT` from any `KeyCode::Char` before dispatch, so the uppercase bindings written as bare `key!('I')` fire from a real key press (verified: `I` runs the handler, `C` prompts `Copy to:`, `S` prompts `Symlink to:`). The handler shells `info --file <path> --output -` and shows the captured stdout -- the Top node only -- via `show_text_in_scratch`, then sets `close_requested`, which now pops the Dired overlay from the non-prompt key path so the scratch buffer is left visible and focused rather than hidden behind Dired.

What still differs from Emacs: the result is an ordinary scratch buffer in `plain text`, not `(Info Narrow)`. Emacs's `(info FILE)` builds `*info* (a2ps) Top` with a live navigation graph; here `n`/`p`/`u`/`l`, `Info-menu` and follow-reference do nothing (`n` and `u` leave the cursor at 1:1). Rendering is info(1)'s raw output, so the node header line `File: ...,  Node: Top,  Next: ...` appears as buffer text where Emacs lifts it into a header-line, and menu entries keep their literal `::` where Emacs hides it and makes the entry a link. Closing this needs a per-buffer major-mode keymap mechanism zmax does not have, since binding `n`/`p`/`u`/`l` in a normal document would collide with editing keys.

Separately, the missing-node case is currently invisible: when `info` exits 0 with empty output the code sets the error `info <name>: no such node or anchor: Top`, and Dired correctly stays open, but Dired's own footer occupies the status line so the message is never rendered. Emacs shows `No such node or anchor: Top` in the echo area at once (and without the `info <name>: ` prefix).

`{` is tabulated-list-narrow-current-column: the column at point loses a character and the rows re-render clipped to the new width, never collapsing past one character. There is no separate column cursor any more: `tabulated-list-mode`'s "current column" is simply the one POINT is in, which is why `tabulated-list-next-column` is a point motion, and that is the model now. BufferMenu carries point's horizontal offset in the row; column_starts derives each column's character offset from the layout format_row actually draws (the mark glyph, the CRM cell when the listing shows it, a space, then the four columns each behind its two-space gap), and current_column is the last column whose start is at or before point. Left/Right (and C-b/C-f) move point along the row; M-Left/M-Right are tabulated-list-previous/next-column, moving point to the start of the neighbouring column and stopping at the ends. The header underlines the column point is in. Unit tested: the derived boundaries line up with the drawn layout at every column's first and last character, the motions land where they should, and `{` on point-in-Size narrows Size and leaves the name column alone.

`M-,` in the emacs preset is xref_pop_marker_stack now, not jump_backward. There is a real xref marker ring now, and it is deliberately NOT the jumplist: vim's jumplist records every jump -- searches, `G`, `%`, a window change -- so popping it after a definition lookup lands wherever the last unrelated jump happened to be, which is the divergence the old note recorded. XREF_MARKERS (zmax-term/src/commands.rs) is a ring only xref pushes to, bounded at emacs's xref-marker-ring-length of 16 with the oldest falling off, and every xref entry point pushes the invocation point as it jumps: goto_impl's single-location arm, its picker's selection callback -- pushed there rather than when the picker opens, so a cancelled pick leaves the ring alone -- and the etags/ggtags path, which is what xref-etags-mode makes `M-.` resolve through. Popping skips markers into buffers that have since been closed, as emacs's markers into a killed buffer are dead, and an empty ring reports "At start of xref history". Unit tested for the bound and the LIFO order.

`M-s f C-s` (dired-isearch-filenames) is a port of Emacs's isearch state machine over a character-addressed position space: point is `(row, byte offset into that row's file name)`, and `isearch-cmds`, `isearch-opoint`, `isearch-barrier`, direction and wrap flags are all carried (zmax-term/src/ui/dired.rs:281-314, 1198-1442, router 2767-2830). Verified key-for-key against GNU Emacs 30.2 driving `dired-isearch-filenames` on the same 7-name fixture: every repeated match inside one file name is its own `C-s` stop (a 13-press `a` walk produces the identical row sequence, 3 stops in `aaa.txt`); typing after a repeat re-searches from the near end of the current match, so it fails in place with "Failing" instead of dragging point back to an earlier row; the first `C-r` only reverses direction and re-finds the same match from the other side (`isearch-repeat-on-direction-change` nil); a repeat past the last match fails once and wraps on the next press (`isearch-wrap-pause` t), and the prompt reproduces Emacs's "Failing"/"Wrapped"/"Overwrapped"/"case-sensitive" annotations and the " backward" suffix. `DEL` pops the command stack, `C-g` quits a successful search to the origin and rubs a failing one back to the last success, case folding follows `isearch-no-upper-case-p`, and `C-s` on an empty pattern takes the previous string off the search ring. Still partial on one point: the intra-name offset exists only while a search is live -- Dired's own point is a row, and `begin_input` opens every search at column 0 of the selected row (dired.rs:1121), while Emacs opens at point. So a search that exits with RET in the middle of a name does not hand its position to the next search: emacs `a C-s C-s RET` then a new search and `a` lands on the second entry, zmax re-matches inside the first one. There is no match-count echo, which is correct -- `isearch-lazy-count` is nil by default.

`M-s f C-M-s` (dired-isearch-filenames-regexp) opens an incremental filename search whose pattern is compiled as an Emacs regexp: `emacs_regexp_to_rust` (zmax-term/src/ui/dired.rs:324) escapes bare `(`, `)`, `|`, `{`, `}` to literals and turns `\(`, `\)`, `\|`, `\{`, `\}` into the operators, maps `\<`/`\>`/`\_<`/`\_>` to `\b`, `` \` ``/`\'` to `\A`/`\z`, drops `\=`, treats a backslash inside `[...]` as a literal member, and returns None for a trailing backslash; an uncompilable pattern leaves the state untouched so point holds (dired.rs:1238-1240). `isearch_no_upper_case` (dired.rs:387) implements `isearch-no-upper-case-p` including the `[:upper:]`/`[:lower:]` check and the odd-backslash rule, and feeds `RegexBuilder::case_insensitive` (dired.rs:1182), so smart case applies. Verified against GNU Emacs 30.2 driven in a pty on a six-file fixture: `gamma|beta` and `ap(p)` are literal and fail with the "Failing" prompt while point holds, `gamma\|beta` alternates, `p{2}` is literal where `p\{2\}` repeats, `2$` anchors, `be[` holds point, lowercase `be` folds to reach `abe.txt` while `Be` stays case-sensitive and reaches `zBeta2`, and `C-s` on an empty pattern pulls the previous string off the regexp ring and moves point to it. Still partial: the incremental re-search anchor differs. Emacs re-searches from the search origin on every keystroke, so `beta\|` matches the empty alternative and snaps point to the top of the buffer, leaving `beta\|gamma` on `gamma.txt`; zmax continues forward from the current match and never moves point back, leaving it on `zbeta.txt` -- same keys, same fixture, valid regexp, different file. zmax also omits Emacs's echo-area sub-states "[incomplete input]", "[Trailing backslash]" and the "Pending" prefix (the "Failing" prefix is present and agrees), anchors `` \` ``/`\'` to the file name rather than to the whole dired buffer, and does not translate syntax classes `\sX`/`\SX`, category classes `\cX`/`\CX` or backreferences `\1`-`\9`, which fail to compile and therefore hold point. Unrelated to this spec but affecting which row a search lands on, zmax sorts the listing case-insensitively where Emacs uses byte order.

The note pre-dated the skip. Both halves of emacs's `isearch-invisible` are implemented, on both search paths. ON (emacs's `open`, the default): the closed folds hiding the match are opened, innermost first, until the line shows -- isearch_settle_folds (zmax-term/src/commands.rs). OFF (`isearch-invisible` nil): a hidden match is SKIPPED and the search carries on to the next visible one, in the command path by re-running the search until the landed-on line is visible (with a seen-set so a buffer whose every match is folded terminates and says so rather than looping), and in the incremental path by Prompt::isearch_skip_invisible, which restores the pre-search fold state before each step so skipping does not leave folds opened behind it.

`}` is tabulated-list-widen-current-column, the mirror of `{`. There is no separate column cursor any more: `tabulated-list-mode`'s "current column" is simply the one POINT is in, which is why `tabulated-list-next-column` is a point motion, and that is the model now. BufferMenu carries point's horizontal offset in the row; column_starts derives each column's character offset from the layout format_row actually draws (the mark glyph, the CRM cell when the listing shows it, a space, then the four columns each behind its two-space gap), and current_column is the last column whose start is at or before point. Left/Right (and C-b/C-f) move point along the row; M-Left/M-Right are tabulated-list-previous/next-column, moving point to the start of the neighbouring column and stopping at the ends. The header underlines the column point is in. Unit tested: the derived boundaries line up with the drawn layout at every column's first and last character, the motions land where they should, and `{` on point-in-Size narrows Size and leaves the name column alone.

Complete Current Statement (Cmd-Shift-Enter) = complete_current_statement, bound under the Emacs major-mode prefix C-c as `C-c ;` — active in Insert, Normal AND Select (spacemacs), so it fires while typing like JetBrains. For a `fn`/`if`/`for`/`while`/`match`/`impl`/... header (line_opens_block) in a brace language (lang_uses_braces), closes any open `(`/`[` then inserts `{ body }` and drops the caret on the indented body line — e.g. `fn tommy()` -> `fn tommy() {<caret>}`, `while (1)` -> `while (1) {<caret>}`. Otherwise closes open brackets/parens, appends the terminator (`;` for semicolon languages via lang_uses_semicolons), and opens an indented line below. Brace vs semicolon are independent axes so brace-but-not-semicolon languages (Go, stryke) still get braces; an unknown/scratch buffer defaults to brace-capable (C-family). Core decision is the pure, unit-tested plan_complete_statement. Line-local heuristic (not full PSI).

`smart_type_completion` (commands.rs) filters the server's completion list to the candidates whose signature names the type the caret is expected to produce. LSP never states that type, so it is read off the line before the caret - an annotated binding (`let x: Foo = `), a C/Java-style declaration (`Foo x = `), a cast, or a return arrow - by `expected_type_before`, with `first_type_word` reducing `&'a mut a::Foo<T>` to `Foo`. Items are kept when their `labelDetails.description` or `detail` names that type as a whole word, so `Foo` does not match `FooBar`. Nothing to filter by leaves the list unfiltered; a type that matches nothing says so instead of silently offering everything. Both readers are unit-tested (`expected_type_comes_off_the_line_before_the_caret`, `type_filter_matches_whole_words_only`).

Both guarantee the code has run before continuing, which is require-module's contract; neither has kakoune's declare-once `provide-module` registry or its 'fails if already evaluating' re-entrancy check.

:vsplit / :vs opens the file in a vertical split (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:61349).

"Make Ctrl+Right and Ctrl+Delete stop at word ends instead of beginnings." zmax has both boundaries as separate commands — `move_next_word_end` (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:414, key:emacs:A-f) and `move_next_word_start` (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:412) — so the choice is which command a key is bound to rather than a global option; the deletion side is `delete_word_forward` (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:1268).

"make it wrap lines at blank characters (tabs and spaces) instead of always at the edge of the screen" = zmax's `soft-wrap.max-wrap` (zmax-core/src/syntax/config.rs:585-592: "Maximum space left free at the end of the line. This space is used to wrap text at word boundaries"), settable with `:set-option soft-wrap.max-wrap N`.

"Automatically indent a newly created line to the same number of tabs and/or spaces as the previous line" = `electric_indent_mode` (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:2571, "Toggle re-indenting the line a newline opens").
"create a backup file by adding a tilde" = vim `backup` + `backupext` (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:544-550, default suffix `~`), applied at zmax-view/src/document.rs:1757-1763.

zmax's `backup_dir` (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:551-556) hosts backups in a directory with the file's path flattened into the name; nano's `backupdir` additionally keeps a uniquely NUMBERED backup per save. zmax keeps one backup plus `patchmode` (editor.rs:566-568) for the pristine original.

"Use bold instead of reverse video for the title bar, status bar, prompt bar, mini bar, key combos, line numbers, and selected text." In zmax every one of those is a theme scope with a `modifiers` list — e.g. runtime/themes/onedark.toml:79-82 `ui.statusline.*` with `modifiers = ["bold"]`, :65-66 `ui.cursor.*`, :53-54 `error`/`warning`. `:theme` selects the theme.
"Automatically hard-wrap the current line when it becomes overlong" = `toggle_auto_fill` (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:1858) wrapping at `text_width` (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:415).
"Do case-sensitive searches by default." = `:set-option search.smart-case false` (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:885-887).

"When a filename given on the command line ends in a colon plus digits and this filename does not exist, then snip the colon plus digits and understand the digits as a line number... repeat... two numbers as line and column" — implemented verbatim at zmax-term/src/args.rs:142-173 (`parse_file` returns early when the literal path exists, then tries `path:row:col`, then `path:row`), and reused by `:open` at zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:826.

"Constantly report the cursor position on the status bar." = `toggle_modeline_position` (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:632); the element is StatusLineElement::Position (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:1014) and it is on by default in the status line config (editor.rs:495).

"Use cut-from-cursor-to-end-of-line by default, instead of cutting the whole line." zmax exposes the two cuts as separate commands (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:1271 and the following entry) instead of a default-mode flag.

"Use this color combination for the status bar when an error message is displayed." = the `error` theme scope (runtime/themes/onedark.toml:54), used for error styling at zmax-term/src/ui/editor.rs:3398.

"Set the target width for justifying and automatic hard-wrapping at this number of columns." = `:set-option text-width N` (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:415), the width `reflow_selections` and `toggle_auto_fill` (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:1858) wrap to.

The which-key / auto-info popup is the surface (zmax-term/src/ui/info.rs:137-138, scopes `ui.text.info` / `ui.popup.info`), but it draws the whole grid with a single style (info.rs:171-173) — descriptions and key combos share one colour.

"Draw a vertical stripe at the given column" = `:set-option rulers [N]` (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:515), or `toggle_fill_column` (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:643, "Toggle a fill-column ruler"). Its colour is the `ui.virtual.ruler` scope (runtime/themes/onedark.toml:60), which is nano's `stripecolor`.

"Save the last hundred search strings and replacement strings and executed commands, so they can be easily reused in later sessions." = zmax's shada file — `:wshada` / `:rshada` persist the command-line and search histories, marks and jumplist (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:41551-41576, zmax-term/src/shada.rs).

"Display a scrollbar on the righthand side of the edit window. It shows the position of the viewport in the buffer and how much of the buffer is covered by the viewport." = `scroll_bar_mode` (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:1186); the bar is drawn with a proportional thumb at zmax-term/src/ui/editor.rs:2899-2914.

zmax's counterpart to nano's two help lines is the which-key / auto-info popup, themed by `ui.text.info` and `ui.popup.info` (zmax-term/src/ui/info.rs:137-138). One style covers the whole grid (info.rs:171-173), so the key combos cannot be given a colour distinct from their descriptions.

"Display line numbers to the left of the text area." = the `LineNumbers` gutter — `toggle_line_numbers` (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:16041) adds/removes it from `gutters.layout` (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:383), and `:set-option line-number absolute|relative` (editor.rs:370) picks the numbering mode. Their colour is `ui.linenr` (zmax-view/src/gutter.rs:544).
"Use vim-style lock-files when editing files." = zmax's vim `swapfile` option (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:585) with `swap_directory` (:586-587 region).

"show information about the current buffer at the bottom of the screen ... filename on the left, followed by an asterisk if the buffer has been modified. On the right ... current line and column number" — every one of those is a zmax status-line element (`FileName`, `FileModificationIndicator`, `Position`, `PositionPercentage`, `TotalLineNumbers`: zmax-view/src/editor.rs:975,981,1014,1020,1023) configured through `:set-option statusline.*` (editor.rs:495). zmax has no separate title row to suppress, so it is not one on/off switch.
"Use this color combination for the mini bar." = the `ui.statusline` theme scope (runtime/themes/onedark.toml:79-82, runtime/themes/acme.toml:9-10).

"Enable mouse support ... mouse clicks can be used to place the cursor, set the mark (with two clicks), and execute shortcuts." = `:set-option mouse` (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:364), with `middle_click_paste` (:.. ) and `mouse_yank_register` alongside it.

"When reading in a file with ^R, insert it into a new buffer by default." = `:new` (empty buffer) followed by `:read` (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:65827-65829); `:open` puts the file in its own buffer directly.

"Don't convert files from DOS format." zmax never converts on read — it detects the file's own line ending (zmax-core/src/line_ending.rs:128) and keeps it (zmax-view/src/document.rs:2043), so nano's noconvert is zmax's unconditional behaviour; `:line-ending` converts when you ask.

"Don't display the two help lines at the bottom of the screen." = `:toggle which-key` / `:toggle auto-info` (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:440,464); zmax's key help is an on-demand popup, not two permanent rows.
"Don't automatically add a newline when a text does not end with one." = `:set-option insert-final-newline false` (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:536), with `trim_final_newlines` (:610).
"Use this color combination for line numbers." = the `ui.linenr` / `ui.linenr.selected` theme scopes (runtime/themes/acme.toml:5-6).

"Save the positions of cursor and anchors between editing sessions." = zmax's shada file marks and jumplist (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:41551-41576); the in-session equivalent is `Editor::last_positions` (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:2016), restored on reopen at editor.rs:3575 and recorded at :3633.

"Use this color combination for the prompt bar." = the scopes the prompt renders with — `ui.text`, `ui.menu`, `ui.menu.selected`, `ui.text.inactive`, `ui.background` (zmax-term/src/ui/prompt.rs:2515-2519).

"Interpret the Delete and Backspace keys differently so that both Backspace and Delete work properly." zmax fixes this by remapping the keys instead of a compatibility switch: `:imap <Del> ...` / `:map ...` (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:59750-59779) or the `[keys.*]` config sections.

"Do regular-expression searches by default. Regular expressions in nano are of the extended type (ERE)." zmax's `search` (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:512) is always a regex search, so this is the default and only mode. Same treatment as the already-mapped nano.function.regexp.

"Save a changed buffer automatically on exit (^X); don't prompt." = `:x` / `:wq` (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs, write-then-quit); `auto_save` (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:408) writes without any exit at all.
"Use this color combination for the indicator alias scrollbar." = the `ui.menu` (track) and `ui.menu.selected` (thumb) theme scopes the scroll bar renders with (zmax-term/src/ui/editor.rs:2900-2901).
"Use this color combination for selected text." = the `ui.selection` theme scope (runtime/themes/acme.toml:7).

"Home jumps to the first non-whitespace character" = `goto_first_nonwhitespace` (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:3746, impl at :3765), bound at key:emacs:A-m. nano's second step — pressing Home again at that position to reach column 0 — is the separate `goto_line_start`; zmax has no one-key alternation between the two.

"Display lines that exceed the screen's width over multiple screen lines." = `soft-wrap.enable` (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:530, zmax-core/src/syntax/config.rs:580-605) or `toggle_soft_wrap` (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:645).

"Use the given program to do spell checking and correcting, instead of using the built-in corrector that calls hunspell(1) or spell(1)." zmax shells out to an external speller (`ispell`, zmax-term/src/commands.rs:1772; the pipe runs `<prog> -a` at zmax-term/src/commands.rs:45529-45547) but the program is a fixed search order aspell -> hunspell -> ispell (commands.rs:45538), not a user-settable command line. `ispell_change_dictionary` sets the dictionary only.

"Use this color combination for highlighting a search match." = the `ui.highlight` theme scope (runtime/themes/onedark.toml:72), resolved for search overlays at zmax-term/src/ui/editor.rs:1864,1911 and used by `doc_search_highlights` (editor.rs:1236).

"showing some state flags: I when auto-indenting, M when the mark is on, L when hard-wrapping, R when recording a macro, and S when soft-wrapping. When the buffer is modified, a star (*)" — zmax puts the equivalents in the status line: `Mode` (editor.rs:966), `Register` (:1032, the recording register), `FileModificationIndicator` (:981), `FileIndentStyle` (:993), configured through `:set-option statusline.*` (:495). There is no single top-right flag strip.
"Use this color combination for the status bar." = the `ui.statusline` family of theme scopes (runtime/themes/onedark.toml:79-82).
"Use this color combination for the vertical guiding stripe." = the `ui.virtual.ruler` theme scope (runtime/themes/onedark.toml:60), the stripe `rulers` (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:515) draws.

"Use a tab size of number columns" = `:set tabstop=N`, which calls `doc.set_tab_width` (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:26827, option registered at zmax-term/src/commands/vim_options_data.rs:327; read back by `Document::tab_width`, zmax-view/src/document.rs:3373). `:indent-style N` (typed.rs:55438) is the separate knob for how wide one indent step is.
"Convert each typed tab to spaces" = `:indent-style N` (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:55438-55440); `convert_indent_to_spaces` (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:562) converts existing indentation.

nano's title bar has no zmax counterpart row (the same reason nano.option.minibar / nano.option.zero are partial here). The nearest themable surfaces are `ui.bufferline` / `ui.bufferline.active` for the buffer-name strip (zmax-term/src/ui/editor.rs:3126) and `ui.statusline` for the bar (zmax-term/src/ui/powerline.rs:203); both accept the named palette plus hex and are selected with `:theme`.

zmax has no per-wrap trim toggle. `:set-option trim-trailing-whitespace` (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:613) strips trailing blanks on write (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:6656, inside write_impl); the justify path `reflow_selections` (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:37033 -> zmax-core/src/wrap.rs:36 `refill_paragraph`) rebuilds each line from its words, so wrapped lines carry no trailing blanks either way. Different trigger from nano's option.
"Save a file by default in Unix format." = `default_line_ending` (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:534), or `:line-ending lf` per document (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:55449-55454).

nano's wordbounds rule (punctuation counts as part of a word) is vim's WORD: `move_next_long_word_start` / `move_prev_long_word_start` (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:416-417) plus the `_end` and `extend_` variants, sitting beside the ordinary word motions (commands.rs:412-414). zmax exposes both rules as separate commands rather than one global option, so the choice is which command a key is bound to.

"Let an unmodified Backspace or Delete erase the marked region (instead of a single character, and without affecting the cutbuffer)." = `delete_selection_noyank` (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:795, "Delete selection without yanking"); `change_selection_noyank` (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:797) is the change variant.

"Hide all elements of the interface (title bar, status bar, and help lines) and use all rows of the terminal for showing the contents of the buffer." = `:toggle render-statusline` (zmax-view/src/editor.rs:498) + `:toggle bufferline` (:519) + `:toggle which-key` (:464); three switches rather than one, and zmax has no title row.

select_register (zmax-term/src/commands.rs:40759) is zmax's `"` prefix: pick the register the NEXT yank/paste acts on. It is one-shot — selected_register is taken by the following command (zmax-term/src/ui/editor.rs:4077) — where ne's clip number persists until it is set again, so there is no standing 'current clip'. :registers lists the registers (typed.rs:59149).

ne AutoPrefs loads a per-extension preferences file whenever a document is opened. zmax's automatic per-file settings come from the nearest .editorconfig, applied by :editorconfig / editorconfig-mode (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:65392), plus per-language settings in languages.toml — a different (and standard) file format, and keyed by glob rather than by extension-named prefs file.

vim `:set binary` / `:set bin` is implemented in ex_set (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:26567-26580): the buffer is written back byte-for-byte, no final newline is added unless 'endoffile' says the original had one, and 'expandtab' is forced off — ne's Binary flag.
:line-ending crlf writes CR+LF at the end of every line, :line-ending lf writes LF (zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:55448) — ne's CRLF flag.

ne DelTabs makes BackSpace/Del remove a tab's worth of spaces. That is vim 'softtabstop' (and 'varsofttabstop'): <BS> deletes back to the previous soft stop in zmax-term/src/commands.rs:34915, with the widths read at commands.rs:2947-2963 and set by `:set softtabstop=N` (vim_options_data.rs:305).

ne EscapeTime sets how long the Escape key waits before it is taken as Escape rather than the start of a sequence. That is vim 'ttimeoutlen' (with 'timeoutlen' as the fallback), implemented for the pending-chord timeout at zmax-term/src/commands/typed.rs:30791-30815 and settable with `:set ttimeoutlen=N` (vim_options_data.rs:350). ne counts tenths of a second, zmax milliseconds.
